title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is a proposed law that promotes developing and sharing AI technology through open-source platforms. It seeks to encourage transparency, collaboration, and broad access to AI tools by offering support, funding, and governance standards for open-source projects.

title: To amend the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to authorize certain assessments by the Director of the Institute and impose requirements on certain memorandums of understanding relating to artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: This policy proposes changes to the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Act so that the Director can conduct specific assessments related to artificial intelligence. It also introduces new rules that require certain memorandums of understanding involving AI to meet defined standards and obligations.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: This act aims to protect families from the high energy costs generated by AI data centers. It proposes measures such as transparent billing, subsidies, or rate regulation to shield household budgets from the impact of AI infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction and operation of new AI data centers to address environmental, security, and ethical concerns. Existing facilities would be required to meet stricter sustainability standards, and the law allows for a review period to reassess future AI infrastructure development.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed U.S. law aimed at regulating how artificial intelligence is developed and used to promote safety, fairness, and accountability. It seeks to set standards and guidelines for AI systems, protect privacy, and ensure that AI technologies operate transparently and responsibly in society.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes safety standards and regulatory requirements for AI‑enabled toys sold to children, ensuring they are designed to protect kids from harm and comply with strict safety guidelines. It mandates that manufacturers disclose the AI behavior, data usage, and risk mitigation measures, and it sets up testing, reporting, and enforcement procedures to safeguard child users.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act establishes strict rules to protect the personal data of minors when AI technologies are used. It requires companies to obtain parental consent, be transparent about data collection, and implement robust security measures to safeguard young users' privacy.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies and organizations that develop or deploy AI systems in China to disclose their AI capabilities, usage patterns, and potential impacts. The act aims to increase transparency, monitor compliance with national regulations, and ensure AI technologies are developed responsibly and ethically.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires AI developers and operators in China to track and disclose the energy consumption of their AI systems. By gathering this data, the law aims to improve energy efficiency and reduce the environmental impact of AI technology.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act sets out rules for creating, using, and sharing AI models, aiming to keep them safe, reliable, and transparent. It requires developers to disclose model details, assess risks, and meet privacy standards, while giving regulators tools to monitor misuse and ensure AI systems align with public interests.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill requires AI developers to create and publish detailed functional bills of materials, listing all components and dependencies of an AI system. It also includes additional provisions aimed at improving transparency and accountability in AI development and deployment.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act aims to create a national program that trains and supports professionals dedicated to building trustworthy, transparent AI systems. It seeks to expand job opportunities, set industry standards, and provide resources for education and research in responsible AI development.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes regulations to minimize the environmental footprint of AI systems, requiring developers to conduct environmental impact assessments and adopt energy‑efficient practices. It also creates a federal AI sustainability certification and promotes research into low‑carbon AI technologies.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The act aims to prevent AI companies from charging excessively high prices for AI services and from manipulating wages in the labor market. It seeks to protect both consumers and workers by enforcing fair pricing and curbing wage-fixing practices in the AI industry.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 is a new law that sets rules for using artificial intelligence in farming, covering everything from how data is collected and used to ensuring that AI systems are safe and reliable. It aims to encourage innovation in agriculture while protecting farmers, the environment, and consumer interests by establishing clear standards and accountability for AI-driven tools.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act aims to boost the use of artificial intelligence across banks, fintechs, and other financial institutions by creating a supportive regulatory framework that encourages experimentation and innovation. It also establishes guidelines for data privacy, risk management, and ethical AI practices to protect consumers while allowing the sector to adopt new technologies.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: This act is designed to boost the use of artificial intelligence in the financial sector by creating clear rules and incentives for innovation. It also aims to protect consumers and maintain market stability while letting banks and fintech firms experiment with AI‑driven products and services.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act is a proposed law aimed at boosting the United States’ competitiveness in AI by expanding funding for AI research, creating new educational programs, and attracting skilled talent from around the world. It also seeks to encourage collaboration between government, academia, and industry to accelerate AI innovation while addressing ethical and workforce development concerns.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act bans the construction and operation of AI data centers on federal land. It aims to preserve those lands for other purposes and prevent the environmental and logistical impacts large AI facilities could bring.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to equip U.S. schools with curriculum, teacher training, and resources that help students understand and responsibly use artificial intelligence. It establishes a federal framework for collaboration among educational agencies, schools, and private partners to ensure equitable access to high‑quality AI instruction across all districts.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students and educators with the knowledge and skills needed to understand and use artificial intelligence responsibly. The act outlines programs and resources to support AI education in schools, ensuring that students are prepared for an AI‑driven future.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed legislative framework that aims to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems in the United States, establishing guidelines for safety, transparency, and accountability. It seeks to balance fostering innovation with protecting public interest by setting standards for risk assessment, data governance, and ethical considerations.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act is designed to help schools safely integrate artificial intelligence tools into teaching and learning. It sets standards for teacher training, student data protection, and clear guidelines for when AI can be used in class.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives recognizes that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center deserves clear information about the project and the power to make local decisions. This policy ensures that residents affected by AI data center development have the right to transparency and local autonomy in shaping outcomes that affect them.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is a U.S. law designed to guide how artificial intelligence is used in programs and services for veterans. It sets rules to make sure AI systems are safe, fair, and transparent, and it requires regular oversight to protect veterans from harm or bias.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026 establishes rules to detect, prevent, and address false or misleading claims made by AI systems that could lead to exploitation. It sets out requirements for verification, transparency, and accountability to protect individuals and organizations from AI‑generated misinformation that could be used for fraudulent or harmful purposes.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 encourages systematic study of how artificial‑intelligence tools are used within the judicial system and sets guidelines to promote safe, fair, and transparent application of AI in court processes. The Act also creates an oversight committee that monitors AI deployments in courts, reviews their compliance with legal standards, and recommends policy adjustments as needed.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The bill requires a report that details how artificial intelligence is used to access unminimized information gathered under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978. It also includes additional provisions related to the broader use of AI in intelligence activities.
